title.narrative: Road Sector Governance and Maintenance Project

description.narrative:
The Lao Road Sector Governance and Maintenance Project will improve the delivery of public service in road asset management. It will cultivate sustainable and efficient road asset management practices by strengthening governance and capacity in planning, financing, and implementing routine and periodic road maintenance. The project will rehabilitate and maintain a total of 327 kilometers (km) of national and local roads in the provinces of Salavan, Xekong and Attapu. It will contribute to the achievement of the government's goal of improving road asset management.
The expected impact of the project will be delivery of public services in road asset management improved. The outcome will be sustainable road maintenance implemented in the provinces of Salavan, Xekong and Attapu. The project will consist of three outputs, (1) governance and practice for road asset management improved; (2) institutional capacity for road asset management strengthened; and (3) road asset rehabilitation and maintenance completed.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: 3. Rehabilitation and maintenance of national and local roads completed. Indicator: 3a. 79km of roads in Savaran Province, 72km of roads in Xekong Province and 167.6km of roads in Attapeu Province are rehabilitated and maintained (2015 baseline:0) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Completed. Total -339.4km (target: 311.1 km) NR20 - CW-1: 56 km, LR6901 -CW-2: 17.5 km, plus 12.1km access NR16 -CW-3: 49 km, plus 11.6km access LR7615 - CW-4: 22.7 km, NR18B -CW-5: 111.9 km, LR9001 - CW-6: 54 km plus 6.4km access (additional works). Data Source: 3a. Quarterly progress reports from project management consultant

Output: 2. Institutional capacity for sustainable road asset management strengthened. Indicator: 2a. 200 staff of MPWT with improved knowledge and skills in sustainable road asset management by 2020 (baseline: N/A) Achievement: 101 Progress/Status: Completed. 2a. Total - 5 training sessions conducted - 1029 staff attended. However, DOR and PMC to continue conduct follow-through activities, such as (i) refresher session, (ii) on-the-job training, (iii) knowledge sharing, (iv) hands-on coaching, and (v) knowledge transfer.
101 staff - about 50% of target - MPWT: male - 8; female - 12 - DPWT: male - 55; female - 4 - PTTI: male - 22; female - 0 Data Source: Training workshop evaluation reports

Output: 2. Institutional capacity for sustainable road asset management strengthened. Indicator: 2c. 6 training courses in routine road maintenance and management provided to communities along project roads by 2019 (baseline N/A) Achievement: 12 Progress/Status: Completed. Training courses in routine road maintenance and management provided. The routine road maintenance courses always part of the any project trainings -eg. HIVAID training, road safety awareness campaign.
Four CBM training courses were provided with 262 people participation. Women were 29 (11%). In addition, eight community awareness campaigns on road safety, HIV/AIDS, human trafficking, etc. associated with road improvements were provided with participants of 42,820 people, including 20,835 women (48.7%). Data Source: Quarterly progress report from project management consultant

Output: 1. Governance and practice for sustainable road asset management improved. Indicator: 1a. Revised axle load control regulation developed by 2018 (baseline: N/A) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Completed. 1a. The draft completed in Nov.2017; the draft final completed in June 2018. Data Source: Quarterly progress report from project management consultant Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Target year: 2018 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: 1. Governance and practice for sustainable road asset management improved. Indicator: 1b. Revised Road Maintenance Fund (RMF) developed by 2018 (baseline: N/A) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Completed. 1b. The Decree on RMF issued on 1 Jun. 2016. The project provided recommendation on the long-term financing plan on 13 June 2018. Updated version was disseminated to DOR on 16 March 2021, and DPC, DOF on 25 March 2021. The project involvement on the revision this is no longer required. Next step is that DOR to incorporate all comments (if any), and submit it to the Secretariat of the Road Fund appointed by the Management Committee of the Road Fund. Data Source: Quarterly progress report from project management consultant Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Target year: 2018 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: 1. Governance and practice for sustainable road asset management improved. Indicator: 1c. A web-based road asset management registry established and made available for public disclosure by 2018 (baseline: N/A) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Completed. 1c. The registry has been established by the Word Bank financed project, the Lao Road Sector Project-Phase I. The system was further strengthened jointly with WB LRSP-Phase II and L3368 RGM project. Additionally, the consultant helped DOR input necessary data in the system. Disclosure was completed in 2017. Data Source: Quarterly progress report from project management consultant Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Target year: 2018 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: 1. Governance and practice for sustainable road asset management improved. Indicator: 1d. Updated performance-based maintenance contract documents, Technical Specifications for Road Construction and Maintenance, Road Design Manual, Road Maintenance Manual prepared, approved and issued by 2021 (baseline: N/A) Achievement: N Progress/Status: Completed. The performance-based maintenance contact documents were developed in 2017. The technical specifications for road construction and maintenance were approved by MPWT in August 2018.
The road design manual was approved by MPWT in August 2018. The final draft road maintenance manual was completed in August 2020 and is under MPWT's approval process. It is expected that the manual was approved by MPWT in February 2021. The PMC has conducted training on PBM contact tender for government staff and contractors in 2017. Data Source: Quarterly progress report from project management consultant Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Target year: 2021 Target value: Y Actual value: N

Output: 2. Institutional capacity for sustainable road asset management strengthened. Indicator: 2b. Private contractors with improved skills in performance based maintenance contract tendering and implementation by 2018 (baseline: N/A) Achievement: N Progress/Status: Completed in 2017. Trainings/workshops on PBM contracts have been conducted by PMC to private contractors in November 2017. 6 contractors (male - 44; female - 0) Data Source: Training workshop evaluation reports Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Target year: 2018 Target value: Y Actual value: N
Sustainable road maintenance in the provinces of Salavan, Xekong and Attapu achieved.

c. Average daily traffic on all project roads increased to 30,000 passenger car units (pcu) (21,600 pcu's in 2014) Achievement: 21600 Progress/Status: Achieved. Number of daily traffic on all the project roads increased significantly after completion of the road maintenance, mainly on the local roads. The peak day was up to 47,739 PCUs.
In December 2021, the PBM for both of national roads and local roads, CW-1 (NR 20), CW-2 (LR6901), CW-3 (NR 16), CW-4 (7615), CW-5 (NR18B), and CW-6 (LR9001) has been completed.
PBM for the section K,80-Km111 of CW-5 (18B) will continue till 2nd of 2022 with VO to the contract.
The rehabilitation works of CW-1 (NR-20), CW-2 (LR 6901), DW-3 (NR16), CW-4 (LR 7615), CW-5 (18B) , and CW-6 (LR 9001) have been substantially completed, and have been handed over to the Employer. Defects Liability Certificates for CW-1, CW-2, CW-3, CW-4, CW-5 and CW-6 have been issued. Data Source: Annual road asset management report of MPWT

a. Percentage of national roads in good condition in target provinces increased to 60% (baseline 40% in 2014) Achievement: 60 Progress/Status: Achieved. The Performance-Based Management Contracts (PBM) formats that designed by the project are being used for maintenance works of the roads country wide. 4 out of 4 national roads (100%) in Salavan province (NR1 H, NR15, NR20, NR13S) are in good condition with double bituminous surface treatment pavement. 4 out of 4 national roads (100% - NR1 H, NR16, NR16B, NR1I) in Sekong are in good condition with BDST pavement. 5 out of 5 national roads (100% - NR16B, NR1J, NR1 I, NR18A, NR18B) in Attapeu are in good condition with OBST pavement.
In December 2021, the PBM for both of national roads and local roads, CW-1 (NR 20), CW-2 (LR6901), CW-3 (NR 16), CW-4 (7615), CW-5 (NR18B), and CW-6 (LR9001) has been completed.
PBM for the section K,80-Km111 of CW-5 (18B) will continue till 2nd of 2022 with VO to the contract.
The rehabilitation works of CW-1 (NR-20), CW-2 (LR 6901), DW-3 (NR16), CW-4 (LR 7615), CW-5 (18B) , and CW-6 (LR 9001) have been substantially completed, and have been handed over to the Employer. Defects Liability Certificates for CW-1, CW-2, CW-3, CW-4, CW-5 and CW-6 have been issued. Data Source: Annual road asset management report of MPWT

b. Percentage of local roads in good condition in target provinces increased to 20% (baseline 6% in 2014) Achievement: 20 Progress/Status: Achieved. 1,437km out of 3,591 km (40%) of the local roads in Salavan are in good condition-usable for both dry and wet seasons. 270km out of 488km (53%) of the local roads in Sekong Province are in good condition-usable for both dry and wet seasons. 1,415km out of 2, 112km (67%) of the local roads in Attapeu Province are in good condition-usable for both dry and wet seasons
In December 2021, the PBM for both of national roads and local roads, CW-1 (NR 20), CW-2 (LR6901), CW-3 (NR 16), CW-4 (7615), CW-5 (NR18B), and CW-6 (LR9001) has been completed.
PBM for the section K,80-Km111 of CW-5 (18B) will continue till 2nd of 2022 with VO to the contract.
The rehabilitation works of CW-1 (NR-20), CW-2 (LR 6901), DW-3 (NR16), CW-4 (LR 7615), CW-5 (18B) , and CW-6 (LR 9001) have been substantially completed, and have been handed over to the Employer. Defects Liability Certificates for CW-1, CW-2, CW-3, CW-4, CW-5 and CW-6 have been issued. Data Source: Annual road asset management report of MPWT
